newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTORCYCLING-CLEAR ROAD AHEAD FOR DOOHAN.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CLEAR ROAD AHEAD FOR DOOHAN.

text.p: World champion Michael Doohan starts the San Marino Grand Prix on Sunday knowing it should be one of the easiest races of his career.
For the first time this season the Australian will not have his Honda team mate and one-time title contender Alex Criville breathing down his neck.
Criville will not race again until at least September after suffering severe hand injuries including a severed artery during practice for last weekend's Dutch Grand Prix at Assen.

By the time the Spaniard returns, Doohan, who is already 68 points clear of Criville and 90 ahead of third-placed Nobuatsu Aoki of Japan, will almost certainly have sealed his fourth straight 500cc crown.
Not only will Doohan be helped by Criville's absence, the Australian is racing on a circuit he enjoys.
He won last year and gave a vote of confidence to the 4.89 km layout which was radically redesigned following the deaths of Formula One drivers Ayrton Senna and Austria's Roland Ratzenberger in 1994.
Even the weather seems to be on Doohan's side. Last year he triumphed in torrential rain, but the forecast is good for this weekend after another bout of bad weather.
With the 500cc title race virtually over, local interest will centre on the 250cc and 125cc championships, where Italians are still very much in contention.
Defending 250cc champion Max Biaggi hopes to bounce back from the disappointment of Assen where he was disqualified for ignoring a stop-and-go penalty.
That penalty cost Biaggi the championship lead, which rests with German Ralf Waldman.
In the 125cc catagory, Italian teenager Valentino Rossi seeks to extend his overall lead with his sixth victory in eight races.
